title: Snail Walk
statement:
A snail sits in the top-left cell of a table with **n** rows and **m** columns. It walks along the border clockwise: right along the top row, down the right column, left along the bottom row and up the left column. It never visits a cell twice, so after one round it continues with the inner part of the table in the same way, until every cell is visited.

Print the numbers in the order the snail visits them.
input:
The first line contains two integers **n** and **m**.

Each of the next n lines contains m integers: the table.
output: Print the n·m numbers in the snail's order on one line, separated by spaces.
hints: Keep four borders: `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`. Walk one side, then move that border inwards.
Be careful with a single remaining row or column: do not walk it twice.
editorial:
Keep the borders top, bottom, left, right. While top ≤ bottom and left ≤ right: walk the top row from left to right, the right column from top+1 to bottom, then (only if top < bottom) the bottom row from right-1 back to left, and (only if left < right) the left column from bottom-1 up to top+1. Then shrink all four borders by one.

Complexity: O(n·m).
